blocks.prompt: 19. If \(a_k\) and \(a_m\) denote two different terms of an A.P., show that its \(n^{\text{th}}\) term is \(a_k + (n - k)\left(\frac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\right)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh proof hai. Humein \(a_n\) ka aisa formula chahiye jo \(a_1\) ki jagah kisi bhi do terms, \(a_k\) aur \(a_m\), se kaam kare.
Plan: do terms se \(d\) nikalna; phir \(a_k\) se \(a_n\) tak \((n - k)\) qadam, har qadam \(d\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_k\) aur \(a_m\) A.P. ki do alag terms hain (\(k \ne m\))
Saabit karna hai: \(a_n = a_k + (n - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\).
Tareeqa: General term \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\) ko \(n = k\) aur \(n = m\) ke liye likhenge. Yeh sawal 10 aur 16 ka aam (general) roop hai.

Dono terms likhein
\[a_k = a_1 + (k - 1)d \quad (1)\]
\[a_m = a_1 + (m - 1)d \quad (2)\]
Kyun: General term mein \(n\) ki jagah \(k\) aur phir \(m\) rakha.

Minus kar ke \(d\) nikalein
\[a_k - a_m = (k - m)d\]
\[d = \dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\]
Kyun: \(a_1\) cancel ho gaya, aur \((k - 1) - (m - 1) = k - m\). Terms alag hain, is liye \(k \ne m\), aur \(k - m\) se divide karna jaiz hai. Matlab: do terms ka farq, positions ke farq se divide karein to \(d\) milta hai.

\(a_n\) ko \(a_k\) se jorein
\[a_n - a_k = [a_1 + (n - 1)d]\]
\[\quad - [a_1 + (k - 1)d]\]
\[= (n - k)d\]
Kyun: Wohi chaal: minus karne se \(a_1\) khatam. Asaan zabaan mein, \(k\)th jagah se \(n\)th jagah tak \((n - k)\) qadam hain.

\(d\) ki value rakhein
\[a_n = a_k + (n - k)d\]
\[= a_k + (n - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\]
Kyun: Upar nikali hui \(d\) ki value rakh di; yehi maangi hui shakal hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\) mein upar aur neeche tarteeb ek jaisi rakhein (\(k\) pehle, \(m\) baad mein); ek jagah ulta karne se sign ghalat ho jayega.

Tasdeeq
\(n = m\): \(a_k + (m - k)\dfrac{a_k - a_m}{k - m} = a_k - (a_k - a_m) = a_m \;\checkmark\)
Kyun: \(\frac{m - k}{k - m} = -1\), is liye formula ne \(n = m\) par bilkul \(a_m\) diya. Formula sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(a_n = a_k + (n - k)\left(\frac{a_k - a_m}{k - m}\right)\).
